types.name: Skill tournaments
types.blurb: Head-to-head or multiplayer skill games. Free rooms usually pay gems, not cash. Real USD almost always requires an entry fee.

types.name: Trivia competitions
types.blurb: Live or async quiz contests. Free daily plays exist on some apps. Prize pools are split among remaining winners.

types.name: Fantasy & sports picks
types.blurb: Daily fantasy freerolls and sweepstakes sportsbooks. Free tickets or free coins can win USD; most large pools are paid-entry.

types.name: Creative contests
types.blurb: Writing, photo, and brand challenges judged on a submission. Some are free; some lock cash prizes behind a membership.

types.name: Forecasting tournaments
types.blurb: Judgement competitions scored on calibrated accuracy. You submit probability estimates, not wagers — nothing is staked and prizes come from sponsors.

types.name: Market competitions
types.blurb: Paper-trading and simulated-investing contests scored on portfolio return. Free to enter; prizes are funded by the operator, not your own stake.

types.name: Tech & data competitions
types.blurb: Hackathons and machine-learning contests with published USD prize pools. Free to enter; winners complete tax and identity checks.

types.name: Directories & forums
types.blurb: Places that list many current contests. Use them to find new promotions, then verify each contest’s own official rules.

types.name: Free pool & league platforms
types.blurb: Free tools for running your own pick’em, survivor, squares, or fantasy league. The platform is free; the prize pot is funded by your group.

verificationLevels.name: Account only
verificationLevels.meaning: Email or social login is enough to play. Prize claims usually still require a matching name and contact info.

verificationLevels.name: Eligibility check
verificationLevels.meaning: Age, residency, and one-account rules are enforced. Winners sign an affidavit or confirm identity before payment.

verificationLevels.name: Full KYC
verificationLevels.meaning: Government photo ID, proof of address, and sometimes a selfie or source-of-funds check before any USD redemption.

verificationLevels.name: Tax paperwork
verificationLevels.meaning: US prizes of $600+ typically require a W-9. Non-US winners may need a W-8BEN. Taxes are the winner’s responsibility.
